scatec-los-prados-namasigue.searched: Searched for a CABEI/BCIE loan document and for Norfund and Scatec disclosures on the Los Prados concession companies; found only project announcements and CABEI press releases about other Honduran solar projects, with no lender terms for this project.

drc-2002-mining-code.conditions_add: Publication of the new mining code was a prior action for DR Congo's three-year IMF arrangement, listed as due "Before end-April 2002" (IMF, Letter of Intent and Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies, April 2002, Table 5). An earlier benchmark, set for 30 September 2001 under the staff-monitored programme, was to "Finalize the investment code and the mining code prepared with World Bank assistance" (Table 2).

why.law: Publication of the new mining code was a prior action for DR Congo's three-year IMF arrangement, listed as due "Before end-April 2002"

sources_add.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Letter of Intent, Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies (13 April 2002)

drc-2002-mining-code.searched: Searched for a World Bank credit document making the code a condition; found no Bank loan covenant, but the IMF letter of intent lists the code's publication as a prior action and the drafting as a benchmark.

lahore-north-grid-station-farmland.conditions_add: ADB's facility administration manual for the programme and its first tranche required a land acquisition and resettlement plan (LARP) for each contract package, to be finalised and submitted to ADB for review, and said that "Clearance of the sectional LARP monitoring reports by ADB is a prerequisite for commencing civil works activities" (ADB, Facility Administration Manual). NTDC also had to "obtain all regulatory clearances from the concerned environmental protection agency (provincial) before starting civil works" and to include environmental management plans in bidding documents. ADB's own monitoring report for Loan 3677 says "the loan covenants require that land acquisition and resettlement instruments be monitored internally and externally".

why.safeguard: Clearance of the sectional LARP monitoring reports by ADB is a prerequisite for commencing civil works activities

sources_add.title: Facility Administration Manual: Pakistan, Second Power Transmission Enhancement Investment Program (Project 48078)
sources_add.publisher: Asian Development Bank (via Early Warning System, Rights in Development)

sources_add.title: Social Monitoring Report: Pakistan, Second Power Transmission Enhancement Investment Program (48078-005)

lahore-north-grid-station-farmland.searched: Read the ADB Special Project Facilitator final report (no covenant text), then the ADB facility administration manual and the tranche 3 social monitoring report, which give the LARP and environmental clearance conditions and refer to the Loan 3677 covenants.

naga-cebu-kepco-coal-dust.searched: Read the ADB Compliance Review Panel final report and searched ADB's project documents for Loan 2612: the loan agreement is not published and the report quotes none of it. Its ash-disposal statement comes from the board report (RRP), not the loan agreement, and the report notes ADB policy only says environmental management plan details 'must also be reflected in the loan agreement' without confirming that happened.

asuncion-metrobus-frentistas.conditions_add: The loan contract's special provisions, clause 3.03(f), required the Ministry of Public Works to sign agreements with the municipalities of Asuncion, San Lorenzo and Fernando de la Mora, and required those agreements to cover plans for communication, relocation, resettlement and economic redevelopment of the affected parties; the report says the agreements were to be signed before contracts were tendered (IDB MICI compliance review report, 2018). MICI also found the programme was approved without an environmental and social management plan and without a resettlement plan; a master plan for involuntary resettlement was prepared in 2016.

why.safeguard: required those agreements to cover plans for communication, relocation, resettlement and economic redevelopment of the affected parties

sources_add.title: Compliance Review Report, PR-MICI002-2016 (PR-L1044)
sources_add.publisher: IDB Independent Consultation and Investigation Mechanism (MICI), via Accountability Console

asuncion-metrobus-frentistas.searched: The iadb.org copy of the MICI report could not be opened; read the same report hosted by Accountability Console, which quotes loan contract clause 3.03(f).

marena-renovables-san-dionisio.conditions_add: The IDB attached an environmental and social action plan to loan ME-L1107, which states that "As per the loan agreement, the client will remain in compliance with IDB's policies" (IDB, action plan status report, 5 December 2011, updated 25 September 2012). Several items had to be done "Prior to financial close", among them updated land acquisition arrangements, finalised right-of-way negotiations and outstanding land use permits. The plan also required at least one consultation session with residents of Santa Maria, San Dionisio and Alvaro Obregon on the construction programme, project scope and mitigation measures, and required the company to set up a grievance mechanism based on IFC good practice and to submit, in form and substance satisfactory to the IDB, management plans for health and safety, traffic, emergencies and the environment.

why.safeguard: Several items had to be done "Prior to financial close", among them updated land acquisition arrangements, finalised right-of-way negotiations and outstanding land use permits
why.admin: required the company to set up a grievance mechanism based on IFC good practice and to submit, in form and substance satisfactory to the IDB, management plans for health and safety, traffic, emergencies and the environment

sources_add.title: Environmental and Social Action Plan status report, Marena Renovables Wind Power Project (ME-L1107)
sources_add.publisher: Inter-American Development Bank (hosted by UNAM, Nacion Multicultural)

marena-renovables-san-dionisio.searched: mici.iadb.org and iadb.org document.cfm could not be opened; found the IDB action plan for ME-L1107 hosted by UNAM.

marsyangdi-corridor-lamjung.conditions_add: The EIB finance contract required the Nepal Electricity Authority to "implement and operate the Project in compliance with the Environmental and Social Standards" and with "the updated Environmental and Social Management Plan and the RIPP", the Resettlement and Indigenous Peoples Plan, and to "obtain, maintain and comply with the requisite Environmental or Social Approvals for the Project" (Article 6.05(e); EIB Complaints Mechanism conclusions report). For each project component, payment of the money required "(A) completion of EIA procedures, and (B) confirmation of environmental approval(s) by the competent national authority in Nepal" (Article 1.04B(iii)). The report also says a final EIA or IEE report and the management plans had to be delivered before any construction activity on transmission lines or associated substations began (Article 8.01 and Schedule A.2).

why.safeguard: the updated Environmental and Social Management Plan and the RIPP

sources_add.title: Conclusions Report, SG/E/2018/39 Nepal Power System Expansion Project

marsyangdi-corridor-lamjung.searched: The 2019 initial assessment report gives no contract wording; the 2024 conclusions report quotes the finance contract articles.

malicounda-power-plant-land.searched: Opened the Early Warning System record for AfDB project P-SN-F00-009 (board date 27 November 2018): no project description, undisclosed risk category and no conditions listed. Searched for an AfDB appraisal report or environmental and social summary for the plant and found only US DFC screening documents and press articles. Also opened the AfDB project page for P-SN-F00-009, which gives only the approval date and amount plus a truncated environmental and social impact study summary, and no loan conditions.

abidjan-fourth-bridge-boribana.searched: Opened the Early Warning System record for AfDB project P-CI-D00-010 (Abidjan urban transport, phase 2) and a government tender for an audit of the project's environmental and social management plan and resettlement action plan. The tender says the audit covers 'l'evaluation du degre de conformite avec les dispositions de l'accord de financement' but does not say the financing agreement required those plans; the AfDB appraisal report was not found.

la-chorrera-pan-am-generating.searched: Read the IDB press release on the US$59.8 million financing: it gives the structure (a US$20.3 million IDB loan plus a US$39.5 million syndicated loan) and notes a five-year power purchase agreement with Empresa de Distribucion Electrica Metro Oeste, but states no guarantees, security or environmental requirements. The MICI case page could not be opened.

morosi-obsidian-coal-dust.searched: Read AidData record 92497: it names Bank of China as security/collateral agent but says the collateral is not identified (AidData only assumes the loan was collateralized), lists no guarantees, no use-of-proceeds restriction and no procurement requirement.

smederevo-hbis-red-dust.searched: Read AidData record 67013: it gives no collateral, guarantee, use-of-proceeds restriction, procurement requirement or Serbian government commitment for the Bank of China loan; interest and maturity are listed as unknown.

obi-kawasi-nickel-hpal.searched: Read DBS's announcement of the US$625 million financing: it describes the structure but names no Equator Principles or IFC Performance Standards, no environmental or social action plan, no tailings or waste conditions, no offtake and no security.

pacitan-coal-plant-fishers.searched: Read the Petromindo report of the loan (US$293.23 million, 12-year tenor, two-year grace) and the Global Energy Monitor page: neither gives an interest rate, a guarantee, a procurement requirement or any other condition attached to the China Exim credit.

tozzi-green-ihorombe.searched: Opened BIO's investment page for JTF Madagascar (EUR 2.9 million debt, November 2019): it lists expected development impacts but no environmental, social, land or other conditions attached to the loan; searched for a BIO/Finnfund action plan for the investment without result.

aswan-high-dam-nubian-displacement.searched: Read the US State Department cables in Foreign Relations of the United States 1958-1960 (documents 223 and 256): they give the 400 million ruble figure and say the Soviet Union would take part in the second stage 'on the same basis as the first stage', but state no interest rate, repayment period, repayment in cotton or goods, or requirement to use Soviet equipment or technicians.

green-resources-uganda-evictions.searched: IFC's project disclosure page could not be opened directly; read IFC's environmental and social review summary for project 26506, which names the Performance Standards applied and the Environmental Action Plan. The action plan PDF itself is not published on that page.

korindo-papua-forest-clearing.searched: Read the RAN/WALHI/TuK-Indonesia/Profundo report 'Perilous': it records BNI loans of about US$190 million to Korindo's agricultural division (Q3 2017) and a 2012 US$40 million SMBC loan with JBIC to PT Korintiga Hutani for wood chips in Kalimantan, but reports no conditions, covenants or sustainability requirements attached to any of these loans; BNI's certification requirement is described as the bank's own general policy.

cdc-pt-hsl-manis-mata.searched: Read the Down to Earth / WALHI Kalbar report on CDC and PT Harapan Sawit Lestari: it records CDC's statutory obligation to work within business principles agreed with the UK Department for International Development and an audit CDC commissioned in mid-2000, after its second investment, but no conditions written into CDC's loan or equity, and no compensation or smallholder-scheme requirement set by CDC.

messok-dja-baka-ecoguards.searched: Read the UNDP SECU final investigation report: the obligations it discusses (social and environmental screening, indigenous peoples safeguards, grievance mechanism) come from UNDP's own Social and Environmental Standards and policy, not from terms of the GEF grant; the grant agreement is not quoted and the project document does not refer to the 2015 standards.

novi-sad-station-canopy-collapse.conditions_add: The international agreements Serbia signed with China Eximbank in May 2017 and April 2019, which Serbia's parliament adopted, "revealed that the modernization of two key railway sections was awarded to a Chinese consortium" of China Railway International and China Communications Construction Company (CHOICE, 2025). The commercial contracts themselves were not accessible; CHOICE says a July 2018 contract covering the section that includes Novi Sad station revealed "the selection of Chinese firms for the project was predetermined before the loan agreements were finalized".

sources_add.title: The Novi Sad Railway Station Collapse: The Cost of Sino-Serbian Infrastructure Deals
sources_add.publisher: China Observers in Central and Eastern Europe (CHOICE)

novi-sad-station-canopy-collapse.searched: Read the CHOICE (China Observers in Central and Eastern Europe) analysis of the railway financing; it describes the contractor award in the loan agreements but does not quote repayment, guarantee or Chinese-content terms, and the ratified agreements themselves are not reproduced.

gezhouba-shieli-cement-kodamanov.conditions_add: The 2017 syndicated loan was backed by the Chinese parent company: AidData records that "China Gezhouba Group Cement Co., Ltd. proved a guarantee for the loan". China's export credit insurer Sinosure provided "overseas investment insurance that covered political risk up to 95%". The loan ran nine years, with the last scheduled repayment on 30 December 2025 (AidData).

why.repay: China Gezhouba Group Cement Co., Ltd. proved a guarantee for the loan

sources_add.title: China Eximbank contributes $64.5 million to $129 million syndicated loan for Shieli cement plant (record 70845)

gezhouba-shieli-cement-kodamanov.searched: Read AidData record 70845 for the loan's security, guarantee and insurance terms.

sahiwal-coal-plant-qadirabad.conditions_add: AidData records the October 2015 buyer's credit as secured by a pledge of the equity holders' shares in the project company, Huaneng Shandong Ruyi (Pakistan) Energy Ltd, and by a PKR 50 billion government cash deposit in an escrow account at the State Bank of Pakistan. Its description also says "The Government of Pakistan also issued a sovereign guarantee in support of the loan", but AidData's own staff notes put this as an assumption - "AidData assumes that the loan captured in this record is backed by a sovereign guarantee" - and record that Pakistan's Ministry of Finance classes all independent power producer debt as private debt. Sinosure insured the credit at a premium of 5.26% (AidData).

why.repay: secured by a pledge of the equity holders' shares in the project company, Huaneng Shandong Ruyi (Pakistan) Energy Ltd

sources_add.title: [CPEC] Bank of China contributes to $1.44 billion syndicated buyer's credit for Sahiwal (record 92302)

sahiwal-coal-plant-qadirabad.searched: Read AidData record 92302 for collateral, guarantees, escrow and insurance terms.

colombo-port-city-negombo-fishers.conditions_add: AidData records the May 2017 China Development Bank loan as "collateralized against CHEC's equity stake in CHEC Port City Colombo (Pvt.) Ltd.", with the project's sales revenues also cited as collateral, and says "The loan is also supported by a Sinosure credit insurance policy". It adds that "No sovereign guarantee was provided by the central government in support of the loan". For the separate US$100 million interest-free loan of April 2019, "the proceeds of the loan were to be used to construct an underground tunnel and access road" (AidData).

why.repay: collateralized against CHEC's equity stake in CHEC Port City Colombo (Pvt.) Ltd.

chancay-port-fishers-houses.conditions_add: AidData records the 15-year syndicated loan signed on 28 March 2023 as secured by the shares of the project company CSP Chancay plus "an all-assets pledge, an accounts pledge, a land and concession mortgage", together with direct agreements with the project's contractors, and names Bank of China as security agent. The loan covers 72.22% of the US$1.3 billion cost of Phase 1 and carries a rate of SOFR plus 1.93% (AidData).

why.repay: an all-assets pledge, an accounts pledge, a land and concession mortgage
